p2.original: Unemployment and the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Complicated Story
p2.zh: 失业与COVID-19大流行:一个复杂的故事

p3.original: It was the most abrupt economic change in the post-World War II era. Between March 2020 and April 2020, the U.S. unemployment rate increased from 4.4% to 14.8%. As a result of the COVID-19 pandemic, millions of people were left without work as businesses shut down and people stayed home and cut their spending, especially on restaurants, tourism, and travel. As confidence and spending were slowly restored, and as the situation with the virus steadily improved, unemployment began to tick down. By 2022, with the availability of vaccines and boosters and other improved health measures, things were better still, but the presence of dangerous variants prevented a full return to normal.
p3.zh: 这是二战后时代最突然的经济变化.2020年3月至2020年4月,美国失业率从4.4%上升至14.8%. 由于COVID-19大流行,数百万人因企业停业而无业,人们留在家中削减开支,特别是餐饮、旅游和旅游。 随着信心和支出的缓慢恢复,随着病毒状况的稳步改善,失业率开始下降。到了2022年,随着疫苗和助推器的提供以及其他改进的卫生措施,情况仍然较好,但危险的变体的存在使得无法完全恢复正常.

p4.original: The COVID-19 pandemic had other effects on the labor market as well. Labor force participation—the rate at which people are employed or actively searching for work—declined and as of early-2022 remained lower than it was in 2019. Some were forced to stop working because of school and childcare closures. Others were concerned about how safe their workplaces would be in the middle of a global pandemic. And still others simply chose to retire early. Labor force participation remains a sore spot in the labor market's recovery.
p4.zh: COVID-19流行病也对劳动力市场产生了其他影响。劳动力参与率——就业率或积极寻找工作率——已下降,截至2022年初仍低于2019年的水平。 由于学校和儿童保育关闭,有些人被迫停止工作。 其他发言者则对其工作场所在全球大流行病中的安全程度表示关切。还有一些人只是选择提前退休。劳动力参与仍然是劳动力市场复苏中的一个痛点。

p5.original: These two statistics—unemployment and labor force participation—show how complicated the labor market can be. As the unemployment rate declined through 2021, the disappointing statistics on labor force participation show weak points. One day you may have read a headline about how easy it was to find a job, and the next day a headline would describe how difficult it was for employers to find workers. By the end of this chapter, you will be in a much better position to make sense of these events.
p5.zh: 这两种统计数字——失业和劳动力参与——显示了劳动力市场的复杂程度。 随着2021年失业率的下降,关于劳动力参与的令人失望的统计数据显示出薄弱点。有一天,你可能读过一条标题,关于找到工作是多么容易,第二天,一条标题将描述雇主找到工人是多么困难。 到本章末,你们将更能了解这些事件。

p12.original: Unemployment can be a terrible and wrenching life experience—like a serious automobile accident or a messy divorce—whose consequences only someone who has gone through it can fully understand. For unemployed individuals and their families, there is the day-to-day financial stress of not knowing from where the next paycheck is coming. There are painful adjustments, like watching your savings account dwindle, selling a car and buying a cheaper one, or moving to a less expensive place to live. Even when the unemployed person finds a new job, it may pay less than the previous one. For many people, their job is an important part of their self worth. When unemployment separates people from the workforce, it can affect family relationships as well as mental and physical health.
p12.zh: 失业可能是一种可怕和痛苦的生活经历,就像严重的汽车事故或混乱的离婚,只有经历过失业的人才能完全理解这种情况的后果。 对于失业个人及其家庭来说,日常财政压力是不知道下一次工资将来自何处。有一些痛苦的调整,比如看着你的储蓄账户不断减少,出售汽车并购买更便宜的汽车,或者搬到一个更便宜的地方居住. 即使失业人员找到了新的工作,其工资也可能低于前一份。 对许多人来说,他们的工作是他们自我价值的一个重要部分. 当失业将人们与劳动力隔离时,它会影响家庭关系以及身心健康。

p13.original: The human costs of unemployment alone would justify making a low level of unemployment an important public policy priority. However, unemployment also includes economic costs to the broader society. When millions of unemployed but willing workers cannot find jobs, economic resource are unused. An economy with high unemployment is like a company operating with a functional but unused factory. The opportunity cost of unemployment is the output that the unemployed workers could have produced.
p13.zh: 仅靠失业的人力成本就有理由将低失业率作为公共政策的重要优先事项。 然而,失业还包括对广大社会的经济代价。 当数百万失业但愿意工作的工人找不到工作时,经济资源就得不到利用。失业率高的经济就像一家在一家运转正常但未得到利用的工厂经营的公司。失业的机会成本是失业工人本可以产生的结果。

p14.original: This chapter will discuss how economists define and compute the unemployment rate. It will examine the patterns of unemployment over time, for the U.S. economy as a whole, for different demographic groups in the U.S. economy, and for other countries. It will then consider an economic explanation for unemployment, and how it explains the patterns of unemployment and suggests public policies for reducing it.
p14.zh: 本章将讨论经济学家如何界定和计算失业率。它将研究随着时间推移,整个美国经济,美国经济中不同的人口群体,以及其他国家失业的规律. 然后,它将考虑对失业的经济解释,以及如何解释失业模式,并提出减少失业的公共政策。

p15.original: How Economists Define and Compute Unemployment Rate
p15.zh: 经济学家如何界定和计算失业率

p16.original: Newspaper or television reports typically describe unemployment as a percentage or a rate. A recent report might have said, for example, from September 2021 to October 2021, the U.S. unemployment rate declined from 4.8% to 4.6%. At a glance, the changes between the percentages may seem small. However, remember that the U.S. economy has about 162 million adults (as of the beginning of 2022) who either have jobs or are looking for them. A rise or fall of just 0.1% in the unemployment rate of 162 million potential workers translates into 160,000 people, which is roughly the total population of a city like Syracuse, New York, Brownsville, Texas, or Pasadena, California. Large rises in the unemployment rate mean large numbers of job losses. In April 2020, at the peak of the pandemic-induced recession, over 20 million people were out of work. Even with the unemployment rate at 4.2% in November 2021, about 7 million people who were looking for jobs were out of work.
p16.zh: 报纸或电视报道通常将失业率描述为百分比或比率。一份近期的报告可能会说,例如从2021年9月至2021年10月,美国的失业率从4.8%下降到4.6%. 从一看,百分比之间的变化似乎不大。 然而,请记住,美国经济约有1.62亿成年人(截至2022年初),他们要么有工作,要么正在寻找工作. 在1.62亿潜在工人的失业率上下只有0.1%,这相当于16万人,大约是锡拉丘兹,纽约,德克萨斯州布朗斯维尔或加利福尼亚州帕萨迪纳等城市的总人口.失业率的大幅上升意味着大量失业。2020年4月,在大流行病引发的衰退高峰期,超过2000万人失业. 即使2021年11月失业率为4.2%,寻找工作的约700万人失业.

p17.original: The Bureau of Labor Statistics tracks and reports all data related to unemployment.

p18.original: Who’s In or Out of the Labor Force?

p19.original: Should we count everyone without a job as unemployed? Of course not. For example, we should not count children as unemployed. Surely, we should not count the retired as unemployed. Many full-time college students have only a part-time job, or no job at all, but it seems inappropriate to count them as suffering the pains of unemployment. Some people are not working because they are rearing children, ill, on vacation, or on parental leave.
p19.zh: 我们是否应该把没有工作的人算作失业? 当然不是。 例如,我们不应把儿童算作失业。 当然,我们不应把退休者算作失业人员。 许多全日制大学生只有兼职工作,或者根本没有工作,但将他们算作失业的痛苦似乎不合适.一些人没有工作,因为他们正在抚养子女、生病、休假或育儿假。

p20.original: The point is that we do not just divide the adult population into employed and unemployed. A third group exists: people who do not have a job, and for some reason—retirement, looking after children, taking a voluntary break before a new job—are not interested in having a job, either. It also includes those who do want a job but have quit looking, often due to discouragement due to their inability to find suitable employment. Economists refer to this third group of those who are not working and not looking for work as out of the labor force or not in the labor force.
p20.zh: 问题在于,我们不仅将成年人分为就业和失业两类。第三个群体是:没有工作的人,由于某种原因——退休、照顾子女、在从事新工作之前自愿休息——对有工作也不感兴趣。 它还包括那些确实希望找到工作但已经停止寻找工作的人,这往往是因为他们无法找到合适的工作而感到沮丧。经济学人指第三类不工作,不寻找工作的人,是脱离劳动大军,或者没有加入劳动大军.

p21.original: The U.S. unemployment rate, which is based on a monthly survey carried out by the U.S. Bureau of the Census, asks a series of questions to divide the adult population into employed, unemployed, or not in the labor force. To be classified as unemployed, a person must be without a job, currently available to work, and actively looking for work in the previous four weeks. Thus, a person who does not have a job but who is not currently available to work or has not actively looked for work in the last four weeks is counted as out of the labor force.
p21.zh: 美国失业率,以美国每月进行的一次调查为依据.人口普查局提出一系列问题,将成年人口分为就业人口、失业人口或非劳动力人口。 要被归类为失业,一个人必须没有工作,目前可以工作,并在前四个星期积极寻找工作。 因此,没有工作但目前无法工作或在过去四周内没有积极寻找工作的人,被计算为劳动力之外。

p22.zh: 就业人员:目前从事有薪工作

p53.original: Even with the “out of the labor force” category, there are still some people who are mislabeled in the categorization of employed, unemployed, or out of the labor force. There are some people who have only part time or temporary jobs, and they are looking for full time and permanent employment that are counted as employed, although they are not employed in the way they would like or need to be. Additionally, there are individuals who are underemployed. This includes those who are trained or skilled for one type or level of work but are working in a lower paying job or one that does not utilize their skills. For example, we would consider an individual with a college degree in finance who is working as a sales clerk underemployed. They are, however, also counted in the employed group. All of these individuals fall under the umbrella of the term “hidden unemployment.” Discouraged workers, those who have stopped looking for employment and, hence, are no longer counted in the unemployed also fall into this group.
p53.zh: 即使属于“劳动力之外”类别,仍有一些人在就业、失业或劳动力的分类中被错误地贴上标签。 有些人只从事兼职或临时工作,他们正在寻找全职和长期就业,这些就业被算作是就业,尽管他们的工作方式不是他们愿意或需要的。 此外,还有一些人就业不足。 这包括受过培训或熟练从事一种或一种工作,但从事报酬较低的工作或没有利用技能的工作的人。 例如,我们将考虑一个拥有大学财务学位的个人,他作为一名销售员从事未充分就业的工作。 然而,他们也在就业群体中被计算在内。 所有这些人都属于“隐性失业”一词的范畴。 受挫工人、不再寻求就业因而不再被计算在失业之列的人也属于这一群体。

p55.original: Another important statistic is the labor force participation rate. This is the percentage of adults in an economy who are either employed or who are unemployed and looking for a job. Using the data in  and , those included in this calculation would be the 162.052 million individuals in the labor force. We calculate the rate by taking the number of people in the labor force, that is, the number employed and the number unemployed, divided by the total adult population and multiplying by 100 to get the percentage.  For the data from November 2021, the labor force participation rate is 61.8%. Historically, the civilian labor force participation rate in the United States climbed beginning in the 1960s as women increasingly entered the workforce, and it peaked at just over 67% in late 1999 to early 2000. Since then, the labor force participation rate has steadily declined, slowly to about 66% in 2008, early in the Great Recession, and then more rapidly during and after that recession. The labor force then climbed slowly during the 2010s but declined again during the pandemic in March–April 2020 and remained lower than pre-pandemic levels as of early 2022.
p55.zh: 另一项重要的统计是劳动力参与率。 这是经济中的成年人就业或失业并寻找工作的百分比。利用其中的数据,计算中包括的劳动力人数为1.62052亿。 我们计算这个比率时,将劳动力人数,即就业人数和失业人数,除以成人人口总数,再乘以100,以获得这个百分比。2021年11月的数据显示,劳动力参与率为61.8%。 从历史上看,美国文职劳动力参与率从1960年代开始上升,因为妇女越来越多地进入劳动力队伍,1999年底至2000年初达到高峰,略高于67%。 此后,劳动力参与率稳步下降,2008年在大衰退初期缓慢下降到约66%,随后在衰退期间和之后更迅速。2010年代,劳动力缓慢攀升,但在2020年3月至4月的大流行期间再次下降,截至2022年初仍低于扩大前的水平。

p57.original: When the unemployment report comes out each month, the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) also reports on the number of jobs created—which comes from the establishment payroll survey. The payroll survey is based on a survey of about 147,000 businesses and government agencies throughout the United States. It generates payroll employment estimates by the following criteria: all employees, average weekly hours worked, and average hourly, weekly, and overtime earnings. One of the criticisms of this survey is that it does not count the self-employed. It also does not make a distinction between new, minimum wage, part time or temporary jobs and full time jobs with “decent” pay.
p57.zh: 每月发表失业报告时,劳工统计局(BLS)也报告创造的就业机会数量——这来自机构工资调查。薪金调查是根据对全美国约147 000家企业和政府机构的调查进行的。 它按照以下标准产生工资雇用估计数:所有雇员、每周平均工作时间和每小时、每周和加班平均收入。本次调查的批评之一是它不计入个体户. 它也没有区分新的最低工资、兼职或临时工作与“体面”薪酬的全职工作。

p58.original: How Does the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics Collect the U.S. Unemployment Data?
p58.zh: 如何是美国.劳工统计局 收集美国.失业数据?

p59.original: The unemployment rate announced by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics on the first Friday of each month for the previous month  is based on the Current Population Survey (CPS), which the Bureau has carried out every month since 1940. The Bureau takes great care to make this survey representative of the country as a whole. The country is first divided into 3,137 areas. The U.S. Bureau of the Census then selects 729 of these areas to survey. It divides the 729 areas into districts of about 300 households each, and divides each district into clusters of about four dwelling units. Every month, Census Bureau employees call about 15,000 of the four-household clusters, for a total of 60,000 households. Employees interview households for four consecutive months, then rotate them out of the survey for eight months, and then interview them again for the same four months the following year, before leaving the sample permanently.
p59.zh: 美国公布的失业率.劳工统计局在上一个月每月第一个星期五根据人口调查(CPS)进行,该局自1940年起每月进行人口调查。该局非常注意使这一调查代表整个国家。国家首先划分为3,137个地区。 美国.人口普查局随后选择了其中729个地区进行调查. 它将729个地区划分为每个地区约300个家庭,将每个地区划分为约4个住宅单元的集群.人口调查局雇员每月拨打约15,000个四户制组群,共计6万户.雇员连续4个月与家庭面谈,然后轮流离开调查8个月,然后在次年再次与家庭面谈4个月,然后永久离开样本。

p60.original: Based on this survey, state, industry, urban and rural areas, gender, age, race or ethnicity, and level of education statistics comprise components that contribute to unemployment rates. A wide variety of other information is available, too. For example, how long have people been unemployed? Did they become unemployed because they quit, or were laid off, or their employer went out of business? Is the unemployed person the only wage earner in the family? The Current Population Survey is a treasure trove of information about employment and unemployment. If you are wondering what the difference is between the CPS and EPS, read the following Clear it Up feature.
p60.zh: 根据这项调查,国家、工业、城市和农村地区、性别、年龄、种族或族裔以及教育程度统计都构成造成失业率的组成部分。 还提供了各种其他信息。 例如,人们失业多久了? 他们是否因为辞职而失业,或被解雇,或雇主断业?失业人员是否是家庭中唯一的挣工资者?目前的人口调查是就业和失业信息的宝库。 如果您想知道CPS和EPS之间的区别,请读以下的 Clear Up 特性 。

p61.original: What is the difference between CPS and EPS?

p62.original: The United States Census Bureau conducts the Current Population Survey (CPS), which measures the percentage of the labor force that is unemployed. The Bureau of Labor Statistics' establishment payroll survey (EPS) is a payroll survey that measures the net change in jobs created for the month.
p62.zh: 美国人口调查局进行目前的人口调查,以衡量失业劳动力的百分比。劳工统计局的建立工资调查是一项工资调查,衡量当月创造的工作岗位的净变化。

p64.original: There are always complications in measuring the number of unemployed. For example, what about people who do not have jobs and would be available to work, but are discouraged by the lack of available jobs in their area and stopped looking? Such people, and their families, may be suffering the pains of unemployment. However, the survey counts them as out of the labor force because they are not actively looking for work. Other people may tell the Census Bureau that they are ready to work and looking for a job but, truly, they are not that eager to work and are not looking very hard at all. They are counted as unemployed, although they might more accurately be classified as out of the labor force. Still other people may have a job, perhaps doing something like yard work, child care, or cleaning houses, but are not reporting the income earned to the tax authorities. They may report being unemployed, when they actually are working.

p68.original: Unemployment imposes high costs. Unemployed individuals experience loss of income and stress. An economy with high unemployment suffers an opportunity cost of unused resources. A person without a job must be willing and able to work and actively looking for work to be counted as unemployed; otherwise, a person without a job is counted as out of the labor force. Economists define the unemployment rate as the number of unemployed persons divided by the number of persons in the labor force (not the overall adult population). The Current Population Survey (CPS) conducted by the United States Census Bureau measures the percentage of the labor force that is unemployed. The establishment payroll survey by the Bureau of Labor Statistics measures the net change in jobs created for the month.

p96.original:
As we look at this data, several patterns stand out:
         Unemployment rates do fluctuate over time. During the deep recessions of the early 1980s, 2007–2009, and 2021, unemployment reached roughly 10%. For comparison, during the 1930s Great Depression, the unemployment rate reached almost 25% of the labor force.
 Unemployment rates in the late 1990s and into the mid-2000s were rather low by historical standards. The unemployment rate was below 5% from 1997 to 2000, and near 5% during almost all of 2006–2007, and 5% or less from September 2015 through March 2020. The previous time unemployment had been less than 5% for three consecutive years was three decades earlier, from 1968 to 1970.
 The unemployment rate never falls all the way to zero. It almost never seems to get below 3%—and it stays that low only for very short periods. (We discuss reasons why this is the case later in this chapter.)
 The timing of rises and falls in unemployment matches fairly well with the timing of upswings and downswings in the overall economy, except that unemployment tends to lag changes in economic activity, and especially so during upswings of the economy following a recession. During periods of recession and depression, unemployment is high. During periods of economic growth, unemployment tends to be lower.
 No significant upward or downward trend in unemployment rates is apparent. This point is especially worth noting because the U.S. population more than quadrupled from 76 million in 1900 to over 324 million by 2017. Moreover, a higher proportion of U.S. adults are now in the paid workforce, because women have entered the paid labor force in significant numbers in recent decades. Women comprised 18% of the paid workforce in 1900 and nearly half of the paid workforce in 2021. However, despite the increased number of workers, as well as other economic events like globalization and the continuous invention of new technologies, the economy has provided jobs without causing any long-term upward or downward trend in unemployment rates.
p96.zh: 当我们看这一数据时,有几种模式突出:失业率确实随时间而波动。 在1980年代初期、2007至2009年和2021年的深度衰退期间,失业率大约达到10%。相比之下,在1930年代的大萧条时期,失业率几乎达到劳动力的25%. 按历史标准计算,1990年代后期和2000年代中期的失业率相当低。 从1997年至2000年,失业率低于5%,在2006-2007年几乎全部期间接近5%,从2015年9月至2020年3月,失业率为5%或更低。上一次连续三年的失业率不到5%,是1968年至1970年的30年前。失业率从来就没有下降到零。 它几乎从来没有达到低于3, 并且它保持低 仅很短的时间。(我们讨论本章后面部分为何如此。 )失业上升和下降的时间与整个经济的上升和下降时间相当吻合,只是失业往往滞后于经济活动的变化,特别是在经济衰退后经济上升期间。 在衰退和萧条期间,失业率很高。 在经济增长时期,失业率往往较低。失业率没有明显上升或下降的趋势。这一点特别值得注意,因为美国人口从1900年的7600万增加到2017年的3.24亿以上,翻了两番多. 此外,美国成年人中现在有较高比例的有薪劳动力,因为近几十年来,妇女大量进入有薪劳动力队伍。1900年妇女占有薪劳动力的18%,2021年占有薪劳动力的近一半。 然而,尽管工人人数增加,以及全球化和新技术不断发明等其他经济事件,但经济提供了工作,没有造成失业率的任何长期上升或下降趋势。

p190.original: However, we need to treat cross-country comparisons of unemployment rates with care, because each country has slightly different definitions of unemployment, survey tools for measuring unemployment, and also different labor markets. For example, Japan’s unemployment rates appear quite low, but Japan’s economy has been mired in slow growth and recession since the late 1980s, and Japan’s unemployment rate probably paints too rosy a picture of its labor market. In Japan, workers who lose their jobs are often quick to exit the labor force and not look for a new job, in which case they are not counted as unemployed. In addition, Japanese firms are often quite reluctant to fire workers, and so firms have substantial numbers of workers who are on reduced hours or officially employed, but doing very little. We can view this Japanese pattern as an unusual method for society to provide support for the unemployed, rather than a sign of a healthy economy.
p190.zh: 然而,我们需要谨慎对待对失业率的跨国比较,因为每个国家对失业的定义、衡量失业的调查工具以及不同的劳动力市场都略有不同。 例如,日本的失业率似乎相当低,但自20世纪80年代末以来,日本经济一直陷入缓慢增长和衰退的泥潭,日本的失业率可能过于高估了日本劳动力市场的景象。 在日本,失去工作的工人往往很快退出劳动力队伍,而不会寻找新的工作,在这种情况下,他们不被视为失业. 此外,日本企业往往很不愿意解雇工人,因此公司有大量工人在缩短工时或正式就业,但做的工作很少. 我们可以将这种日本模式视为社会为失业者提供支助的一种不寻常的方法,而不是健康经济的标志.

p192.original: Comparing unemployment rates in the United States and other high-income economies with unemployment rates in Latin America, Africa, Eastern Europe, and Asia is very difficult. One reason is that the statistical agencies in many poorer countries lack the resources and technical capabilities of the U.S. Bureau of the Census. However, a more difficult problem with international comparisons is that in many low-income countries, most workers are not involved in the labor market through an employer who pays them regularly. Instead, workers in these countries are engaged in short-term work, subsistence activities, and barter. Moreover, the effect of unemployment is very different in high-income and low-income countries. Unemployed workers in the developed economies have access to various government programs like unemployment insurance, welfare, and food stamps. Such programs may barely exist in poorer countries. Although unemployment is a serious problem in many low-income countries, it manifests itself in a different way than in high-income countries.
p192.zh: 将美国和其他高收入经济体的失业率与拉丁美洲、非洲、东欧和亚洲的失业率相比较是非常困难的。其中一个原因是许多较贫穷国家的统计机构缺乏美国的资源和技术能力.人口普查局. 然而,国际比较的一个更困难的问题是,在许多低收入国家,大多数工人没有通过定期支付工资的雇主参与劳动力市场。 相反,这些国家的工人从事的是短期工作、生计活动和易货。 此外,在高收入和低收入国家,失业的影响也大不相同。发达经济体的失业工人可以参加各种政府方案,如失业保险、福利和粮票。 这种方案在较贫穷的国家可能几乎没有。 虽然失业在许多低收入国家是一个严重问题,但表现方式与高收入国家不同。

p194.original: The U.S. unemployment rate rises during periods of recession and depression, but falls back to the range of 4% to 6% when the economy is strong. The unemployment rate never falls to zero. Despite enormous growth in the size of the U.S. population and labor force in the twentieth century, along with other major trends like globalization and new technology, the unemployment rate shows no long-term rising trend.
p194.zh: 美国失业率在经济衰退和萧条时期有所上升,但在经济强劲时又回落到4%至6%之间.失业率从未降至零。 尽管20世纪美国人口和劳动力规模大幅增长,加上全球化和新技术等其他主要趋势,失业率并没有显示出长期上升的趋势.

p195.original: Unemployment rates differ by group: higher for African-Americans and Hispanic people than for White people; higher for less educated than more educated; higher for the young than the middle-aged. Women’s unemployment rates used to be higher than men’s, but in recent years men’s and women’s unemployment rates have been very similar. In recent years, unemployment rates in the United States have compared favorably with unemployment rates in most other high-income economies.
p195.zh: 失业率因群体而异:非裔美国人和西班牙裔人的失业率高于白人;受教育程度低的人的失业率高于受教育程度高的人;年轻人的失业率高于中年人.妇女的失业率曾经高于男子,但近年来男子和妇女的失业率非常相似。 近年来,美国的失业率与大多数其他高收入经济体的失业率相比是有利的。

p197.original: Over the long term, has the U.S. unemployment rate generally trended up, trended down, or remained at basically the same level?
p197.zh: 从长远来看,美国的失业率是总体呈上升趋势,还是呈下降趋势,还是基本保持同一水平?

p198.original: Over the long term, the U.S. unemployment rate has remained basically the same level.
p198.zh: 从长远来看,美国的失业率基本保持不变。

p199.original:
Whose unemployment rates are commonly higher in the U.S. economy:
        
 White or non-White people?
 The young or the middle-aged?
 College graduates or high school graduates?
p199.zh: 在美国经济中,谁的失业率通常较高:白人还是非白人?年轻还是中年?大学毕业生还是高中毕业生?

p200.original:
Non-White people
The young 
High school graduates
p200.zh: 非白人 年轻的高中毕业生

p202.original: Are U.S. unemployment rates typically higher, lower, or about the same as unemployment rates in other high-income countries?
p202.zh: 美国的失业率一般较高、较低,还是与其他高收入国家的失业率大致相同?

p203.original: Are U.S. unemployment rates distributed evenly across the population?
p203.zh: 美国的失业率是否在人口中分布均匀?

p205.original: Is the higher unemployment rates for minority workers necessarily an indication of discrimination? What could be some other reasons for the higher unemployment rate?
p205.zh: 少数群体工人失业率较高是否必然表明存在歧视?失业率上升的其他原因是什么?

p206.original: While unemployment is highly negatively correlated with the level of economic activity, in the real world it responds with a lag. In other words, firms do not immediately lay off workers in response to a sales decline. They wait a while before responding. Similarly, firms do not immediately hire workers when sales pick up. What do you think accounts for the lag in response time?
p206.zh: 虽然失业与经济活动水平有着高度的负面关系,但在现实世界中,失业反应滞后。换句话说,企业不会为了应付销售下降而立即解雇工人。 他们等待一段时间后再回复。 同样,公司在销售量上升时不会立即雇用工人。 你觉得反应时间的滞后会是什么原因?

p207.original: Why do you think that unemployment rates are lower for individuals with more education?
p207.zh: 为什么您认为受教育程度较高的个人失业率较低?

p208.original: What Causes Changes in Unemployment over the Short Run
p208.zh: 短跑导致失业变化的原因

p209.original: We have seen that unemployment varies across times and places. What causes changes in unemployment? There are different answers in the short run and in the long run. Let's look at the short run first.
p209.zh: 我们看到,失业率因时间和地点而异。是什么原因导致失业情况发生变化? 从短期和长期来看,答案各不相同。 先观短行.

p211.original: Let’s make the plausible assumption that in the short run, from a few months to a few years, the quantity of hours that the average person is willing to work for a given wage does not change much, so the labor supply curve does not shift much. In addition, make the standard ceteris paribus assumption that there is no substantial short-term change in the age structure of the labor force, institutions and laws affecting the labor market, or other possibly relevant factors.
p211.zh: 让我们假设,从短期来看,从几个月到几年,一般人愿意为某一工资工作的时间数量不会发生多大变化,因此劳动力供给曲线不会发生多大变化。 此外,让标准ceteris paribus假设劳动力的年龄结构、影响劳动力市场的机构和法律或其他可能的相关因素没有重大的短期变化。

p212.original: One primary determinant of the demand for labor from firms is how they perceive the state of the macro economy. If firms believe that business is expanding, then at any given wage they will desire to hire a greater quantity of labor, and the labor demand curve shifts to the right. Conversely, if firms perceive that the economy is slowing down or entering a recession, then they will wish to hire a lower quantity of labor at any given wage, and the labor demand curve will shift to the left.  Economists call the variation in unemployment that the economy causes moving from expansion to recession or from recession to expansion (i.e. the business cycle) cyclical unemployment.
p212.zh: 企业对劳动力的需求的一个主要决定因素是它们对宏观经济状况的看法。 如果企业认为企业正在扩张,那么它们就愿意以任何工资雇用更多的劳动力,而劳动力需求曲线会转向右倾。 相反,如果企业认为经济正在放缓或进入衰退,那么它们希望以任何特定工资雇用较少的劳动力,劳动力需求曲线将转向左。经济学家称,经济导致的失业变化从扩张转向衰退,或从衰退转向扩张(即商业周期)周期性失业。

p213.original: From the standpoint of the supply-and-demand model of competitive and flexible labor markets, unemployment represents something of a puzzle. In a supply-and-demand model of a labor market, as  illustrates, the labor market should move toward an equilibrium wage and quantity. At the equilibrium wage (We), the equilibrium quantity (Qe) of labor supplied by workers should be equal to the quantity of labor demanded by employers.
p213.zh: 从竞争性和灵活的劳动力市场的供求模式的角度来看,失业是一个谜。 如所示,在劳动力市场的供求模式中,劳动力市场应当朝着工资和数量平衡的方向发展。 在平衡工资(我们)下,工人提供的劳动力的平衡数量(Qe)应当与雇主要求的劳动力数量相等.

p214.original: The Unemployment and Equilibrium in the Labor Market
p214.zh: 劳动力市场中的失业和平衡

p215.original: One possibility for unemployment is that people who are unemployed are those who are not willing to work at the current equilibrium wage, say $10 an hour, but would be willing to work at a higher wage, like $20 per hour. The monthly Current Population Survey would count these people as unemployed, because they say they are ready and looking for work (at $20 per hour). However, from an economist’s perspective, these people are choosing to be unemployed.
p215.zh: 失业的一种可能性是,失业者是不愿意按目前均衡工资工作的人,说每小时10美元,但愿意以较高工资工作,如每小时20美元。月度人口调查将把这些人算作失业人员,因为他们说他们已经准备好寻找工作(每小时20美元)。 然而,从经济学家的角度来看,这些人选择失业。

p216.original: Probably a few people are unemployed because of unrealistic expectations about wages, but they do not represent the majority of the unemployed. Instead, unemployed people often have friends or acquaintances of similar skill levels who are employed, and the unemployed would be willing to work at the jobs and wages similar to what those people are receiving. However, the employers of their friends and acquaintances do not seem to be hiring. In other words, these people are involuntarily unemployed.  What causes involuntary unemployment?
p216.zh: 可能有几个人因为对工资的不切实际的预期而失业,但他们并不代表大多数失业者。 相反,失业人员往往有同样技能水平的朋友或熟人在工作,失业人员愿意从事与这些人所得相似的工作,并获得与之相类似的工资。 然而,他们的朋友和熟人的雇主似乎没有在雇用他们。换句话说,这些人非自愿失业。是什么导致非自愿失业的?

p217.original: Why Wages Might Be Sticky Downward
p217.zh: 工资为何可能粘着向下走

p218.original: If a labor market model with flexible wages does not describe unemployment very well—because it predicts that anyone willing to work at the going wage can always find a job—then it may prove useful to consider economic models in which wages are not flexible or adjust only very slowly. In particular, even though wage increases may occur with relative ease, wage decreases are few and far between.
p218.zh: 如果一个工资灵活的劳动力市场模式不能很好地描述失业问题,因为它预测,任何愿意按持续工资工作的人总是能够找到工作,那么,考虑那些工资不灵活或仅非常缓慢地调整的经济模式可能是有益的。特别是,尽管工资增长可能相对容易,但工资的下降却很少,而且相距甚远。

p219.original: One set of reasons why wages may be “sticky downward,” as economists put it, involves economic laws and institutions. For low-skilled workers receiving minimum wage, it is illegal to reduce their wages. For union workers operating under a multiyear contract with a company, wage cuts might violate the contract and create a labor dispute or a strike. However, minimum wages and union contracts are not a sufficient reason why wages would be sticky downward for the U.S. economy as a whole. After all, out of the 73.3 million or so employed workers in the U.S. economy who earn wages by the hour, only about 1.1 million—less than 2% of the total—do not receive compensation above the minimum wage. Similarly, labor unions represent only about 12% of American wage and salary workers. In other high-income countries, more workers may have their wages determined by unions or the minimum wage may be set at a level that applies to a larger share of workers. However, for the United States, these two factors combined affect only about 15% or less of the labor force.
p219.zh: 经济学家认为,工资可能“僵硬”下行的原因之一是经济法律和制度。 对领取最低工资的低技能工人来说,降低工资是非法的。 对于与公司签订多年合同的工会工人来说,削减工资可能违反合同,造成劳资纠纷或罢工。 然而,最低工资和工会合同并不能成为整个美国经济工资下行粘滞的充足理由.毕竟,在美国经济中大约7 330万就业工人中,他们小时工资,只有大约110万人——不到总数的2%——得不到超过最低工资的补偿。 同样,工会只占美国工资和薪水工人的12%左右. 在其他高收入国家,更多的工人的工资可能由工会决定,或者最低工资可能设定为适用于较大比例工人的水平。 然而,对于美国来说,这两个因素加在一起只影响到大约15%或更少的劳动力.

p220.original: Economists looking for reasons why wages might be sticky downwards have focused on factors that may characterize most labor relationships in the economy, not just a few. Many have proposed a number of different theories, but they share a common tone.
p220.zh: 经济学家们寻找工资可能粘滞在下的原因,侧重于经济中大多数劳工关系可能具有特征的因素,而不仅仅是少数因素。许多人提出了许多不同的理论,但他们有着共同的基调.

p221.original: One argument is that even employees who are not union members often work under an implicit contract, which is that the employer will try to keep wages from falling when the economy is weak or the business is having trouble, and the employee will not expect huge salary increases when the economy or the business is strong. This wage-setting behavior acts like a form of insurance: the employee has some protection against wage declines in bad times, but pays for that protection with lower wages in good times. Clearly, this sort of implicit contract means that firms will be hesitant to cut wages, lest workers feel betrayed and work less hard or even leave the firm.
p221.zh: 一种观点认为,即使不是工会会员的雇员也常常根据隐含的合同工作,这就是当经济疲软或企业出现困难时,雇主会试图防止工资下降,而当经济或企业强大时,雇员也不会预期工资会大幅上涨. 这种确定工资的行为表现为一种保险形式:雇员在不好的时候有某种保护来防止工资下降,但是在好的时候用较低的工资来支付这种保护. 显然,这种隐含的合同意味着公司对削减工资会犹豫不决,以免工人感到被出卖,工作得不那么辛苦,甚至离开公司。

p222.original: Efficiency wage theory argues that workers' productivity depends on their pay, and so employers will often find it worthwhile to pay their employees somewhat more than market conditions might dictate. One reason is that employees who receive better pay than others will be more productive because they recognize that if they were to lose their current jobs, they would suffer a decline in salary. As a result, they are motivated to work harder and to stay with the current employer. In addition, employers know that it is costly and time-consuming to hire and train new employees, so they would prefer to pay workers a little extra now rather than to lose them and have to hire and train new workers. Thus, by avoiding wage cuts, the employer minimizes costs of training and hiring new workers, and reaps the benefits of well-motivated employees.
p222.zh: 效率工资理论认为,工人的生产力取决于他们的工资,因此雇主往往会发现,付给雇员的工资比市场条件可能要求的多一些。其中一个原因是,工资比其他人高的雇员将更有成效,因为他们认识到,如果失去现在的工作,他们的工资将下降。 因此,他们有动力更加努力地工作并留在目前的雇主身边。 此外,雇主知道,雇用和培训新雇员既费钱又费时,因此他们现在宁愿给工人多付一点工资,而不是失去他们,不得不雇用和培训新工人。 因此,通过避免削减工资,雇主将培训和雇用新工人的费用降至最低,并获得有良好动机的雇员的利益。

p223.original: The adverse selection of wage cuts argument points out that if an employer reacts to poor business conditions by reducing wages for all workers, then the best workers, those with the best employment alternatives at other firms, are the most likely to leave. The least attractive workers, with fewer employment alternatives, are more likely to stay. Consequently, firms are more likely to choose which workers should depart, through layoffs and firings, rather than trimming wages across the board. Sometimes companies that are experiencing difficult times can persuade workers to take a pay cut for the short term, and still retain most of the firm’s workers. However, it is far more typical for companies to lay off some workers, rather than to cut wages for everyone.
p223.zh: 不利地选择削减工资的论点指出,如果雇主通过降低所有工人的工资来应对恶劣的商业条件,那么最好的工人,即其他公司中具有最佳就业选择的人,最有可能离开。 最没有吸引力的工人,加上就业机会较少,更有可能留下。 因此,公司更可能通过裁员和解雇来选择哪些工人应该离开,而不是全面削减工资。 有时,面临困难的公司可以说服工人在短期内削减工资,但仍保留公司的大部分工人。 然而,公司解雇一些工人,而不是削减每个人的工资,则更为典型。

p224.original: The insider-outsider model of the labor force, in simple terms, argues that those already working for firms are “insiders,” while new employees, at least for a time, are “outsiders.” A firm depends on its insiders to keep the organization running smoothly, to be familiar with routine procedures, and to train new employees. However, cutting wages will alienate the insiders and damage the firm’s productivity and prospects.
p224.zh: 简单来说,劳动力的内向型模式认为,已经为企业工作的人是“内向型 ” , 而新员工,至少有一段时间是“外向型 ” 。 一家企业依赖内向型企业来保持组织运行的顺利,熟悉常规程序,并培训新员工。 然而,削减工资将疏远内部人士,损害公司的生产力和前景。

p225.original: Finally, the relative wage coordination argument points out that even if most workers were hypothetically willing to see a decline in their own wages in bad economic times as long as everyone else also experiences such a decline, there is no obvious way for a decentralized economy to implement such a plan. Instead, workers confronted with the possibility of a wage cut will worry that other workers will not have such a wage cut, and so a wage cut means being worse off both in absolute terms and relative to others. As a result, workers fight hard against wage cuts.
p225.zh: 最后,相对工资协调的论点指出,即使大多数工人假设愿意看到他们在糟糕的经济时期工资下降,只要其他人也经历这样的下降,但分散经济没有执行这种计划的明显办法。 相反,面临削减工资可能性的工人会担心其他工人不会得到这样的削减工资,因此,削减工资意味着在绝对值和相对于其他人而言都更加糟糕。 因此,工人们极力反对削减工资。

p226.original: These theories of why wages tend not to move downward differ in their logic and their implications, and figuring out the strengths and weaknesses of each theory is an ongoing subject of research and controversy among economists. All tend to imply that wages will decline only very slowly, if at all, even when the economy or a business is having tough times. When wages are inflexible and unlikely to fall, then either short-run or long-run unemployment can result.  illustrates this.
p226.zh: 这些关于工资为何不向下走的理论在逻辑和意义上往往有所不同,而找出每一种理论的优缺点是经济学家不断研究和争论的课题.所有这些都倾向于暗示,即使经济或企业处于艰难时期,工资的下降也只有非常缓慢,即使有的话。 如果工资不灵活,不可能下降,那么短期或长期失业就会产生这种情况。

p227.original: Sticky Wages in the Labor Market
p227.zh: 劳动力市场的粘滞工资

p228.original: shows the interaction between shifts in labor demand and wages that are sticky downward.  (a) illustrates the situation in which the demand for labor shifts to the right from D0 to D1. In this case, the equilibrium wage rises from W0 to W1 and the equilibrium quantity of labor hired increases from Q0 to Q1. It does not hurt employee morale at all for wages to rise.
p228.zh: 显示劳动力需求变化与工资波动之间的相互作用,这些变化是粘滞的。(a) 说明劳动力需求从D0转向D1的情况。 在这种情况下,平衡工资从W0提高到W1,而雇用的劳动力的平衡数量从Q0提高到Q1。工资上涨丝毫不会损害雇员的士气。

p229.original: (b) shows the situation in which the demand for labor shifts to the left, from D0 to D1, as it would tend to do in a recession. Because wages are sticky downward, they do not adjust toward what would have been the new equilibrium wage (W1), at least not in the short run. Instead, after the shift in the labor demand curve, the same quantity of workers is willing to work at that wage as before; however, the quantity of workers demanded at that wage has declined from the original equilibrium (Q0) to Q2. The gap between the original equilibrium quantity (Q0) and the new quantity demanded of labor (Q2) represents workers who would be willing to work at the going wage but cannot find jobs. The gap represents the economic meaning of unemployment.
p229.zh: (b) 说明劳动力需求从D0转向D1的情况,这在经济衰退时往往如此。 由于工资的粘滞性下降,它们不会适应新的平衡工资(W1),至少在短期内不会。 相反,在劳动力需求曲线发生转变后,同样数量的工人愿意按该工资工作;然而,要求按该工资工作的工人数量已从原来的平衡(Q0)下降到了问题2。最初的平衡数量(Q0)与要求的劳动力新数量(Q2)之间的差距代表着愿意按持续工资工作但找不到工作的工人。 这一差距代表了失业的经济意义。

p230.original: Rising Wage and Low Unemployment: Where Is the Unemployment in Supply and Demand?
p230.zh: 工资上升和低失业率:供求失业在哪里?

p231.original: This analysis helps to explain the connection that we noted earlier: that unemployment tends to rise in recessions and to decline during expansions. The overall state of the economy shifts the labor demand curve and, combined with wages that are sticky downwards, unemployment changes. The rise in unemployment that occurs because of a recession is cyclical unemployment.
p231.zh: 这一分析有助于解释我们先前指出的联系:失业往往在衰退中上升,在扩张期间下降。经济的总体状况改变了劳动力需求曲线,加上工资粘滞下降,失业率也随之变化。经济衰退导致的失业率上升,是周期性失业。

p232.original: The St. Louis Federal Reserve Bank is the best resource for macroeconomic time series data, known as the Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED). FRED provides complete data sets on various measures of the unemployment rate as well as the monthly Bureau of Labor Statistics report on the results of the household and employment surveys.
p232.zh: 圣号.路易斯联邦储备银行是宏观经济时序数据的最佳资源,被称为联邦储备经济数据(FRED).联邦人口普查和人口普查局提供关于各种衡量失业率的完整数据集以及关于家庭和就业调查结果的劳工统计局月度报告。

p234.original: Cyclical unemployment rises and falls with the business cycle. In a labor market with flexible wages, wages will adjust in such a market so that quantity demanded of labor always equals the quantity supplied of labor at the equilibrium wage. Economists have proposed many theories for why wages might not be flexible, but instead may adjust only in a “sticky” way, especially when it comes to downward adjustments: implicit contracts, efficiency wage theory, adverse selection of wage cuts, insider-outsider model, and relative wage coordination.
p234.zh: 循环失业随商业周期而上升和下降。在一个工资灵活的劳动力市场,工资将在这样一个市场中进行调整,使所需劳动力的数量始终与所提供劳动力的平衡工资数量相等。经济学家们提出了许多理论,说明为什么工资可能不灵活,而只能以“僵硬”的方式调整,特别是在下调方面:隐含的合同、效率工资理论、不利的削减工资选择、内向型模式以及相对工资协调。

p236.original: Beginning in the 1970s and continuing for three decades, women entered the U.S. labor force in a big way. If we assume that wages are sticky in a downward direction, but that around 1970 the demand for labor equaled the supply of labor at the current wage rate, what do you imagine happened to the wage rate, employment, and unemployment as a result of increased labor force participation?
p236.zh: 从20世纪70年代开始,持续了30年,女性大量进入美国劳动力队伍. 如果我们假设工资呈下降趋势,但大约1970年左右对劳动力的需求相当于按目前工资率提供的劳动力,那么,由于劳动力参与率的提高,工资率、就业和失业情况会如何?

p237.original: Because of the influx of women into the labor market, the supply of labor shifts to the right. Since wages are sticky downward, the increased supply of labor causes an increase in people looking for jobs (Qs), but no change in the number of jobs available (Qe). As a result, unemployment increases by the amount of the increase in the labor supply. This can be seen in the following figure.
p237.zh: 由于妇女涌入劳动力市场,劳动力的供应转向了右翼。 由于工资粘滞,劳动力供应的增加导致寻找工作的人增加(Qs),但现有工作数量没有变化(Qe). 因此,失业人数增加了劳动力供应的增加。 从下图中可以看出这一点。

p238.original: Over time, as labor demand grows, the unemployment will decline and eventually wages will begin to increase again. But this increase in labor demand goes beyond the scope of this problem.
p238.zh: 随着时间推移,随着劳动力需求的增长,失业率将下降,最终工资将再次增加。 但是,劳动力需求的增长超出了这一问题的范围。

p240.original: When would you expect cyclical unemployment to be rising? Falling?
p240.zh: 周期性失业何时会上升?掉下来?

p241.original: Why is there unemployment in a labor market with flexible wages?
p241.zh: 劳动力市场上为什么存在工资灵活的失业问题?

p242.original: Name and explain some of the reasons why wages are likely to be sticky, especially in downward adjustments.
p242.zh: 名称和解释工资可能粘滞的一些原因,特别是在向下调整时。

p244.original: Do you think it is rational for workers to prefer sticky wages to wage cuts, when the consequence of sticky wages is unemployment for some workers? Why or why not? How do the reasons for sticky wages explained in this section apply to your argument?
p244.zh: 你认为当粘滞工资的后果是一些工人失业时,工人选择粘滞工资而不是削减工资是否合理? 为什么或为什么不呢? 本节解释的粘性工资理由如何适用于你的论点?

p246.original: A government passes a family-friendly law that no companies can have evening, nighttime, or weekend hours, so that everyone can be home with their families during these times. Analyze the effect of this law using a demand and supply diagram for the labor market: first assuming that wages are flexible, and then assuming that wages are sticky downward.
p246.zh: 政府通过一部关爱家庭的法律,任何公司都不能有晚上、晚上或周末的时间,这样,在这段时间里,每个人都可以和家人一起回家。利用劳动力市场供需图分析该法的影响:首先假设工资是灵活的,然后假设工资是粘滞的。

p247.original: What Causes Changes in Unemployment over the Long Run

p248.original: Cyclical unemployment explains why unemployment rises during a recession and falls during an economic expansion, but what explains the remaining level of unemployment even in good economic times? Why is the unemployment rate never zero? Even when the U.S. economy is growing strongly, the unemployment rate only rarely dips as low as 4%. Moreover, the discussion earlier in this chapter pointed out that unemployment rates in many European countries like Italy, France, and Germany have often been remarkably high at various times in the last few decades. Why does some level of unemployment persist even when economies are growing strongly? Why are unemployment rates continually higher in certain economies, through good economic years and bad? Economists have a term to describe the remaining level of unemployment that occurs even when the economy is healthy: they call it the natural rate of unemployment.
p248.zh: 循环失业解释了为何经济衰退期间失业率上升,经济扩张期间失业率下降,但为何即使在良好的经济时期,失业水平依然如此?为何失业率从零到零? 即使美国经济强劲增长,失业率也很少下降至4%。 此外,本章前面的讨论指出,在过去几十年中,意大利、法国和德国等许多欧洲国家的失业率往往在不同时期都很高。即使在经济强劲增长的情况下,为什么仍然有一定程度的失业? 为什么某些经济体的失业率通过良好的经济年限和糟糕的年限而持续上升?经济学家有一个术语来描述即使在经济健康时仍然会出现的失业水平:他们称之为自然失业率.

p249.original: The Long Run: The Natural Rate of Unemployment

p250.original: The natural rate of unemployment is not “natural” in the sense that water freezes at 32 degrees Fahrenheit or boils at 212 degrees Fahrenheit. It is not a physical and unchanging law of nature. Instead, it is only the “natural” rate because it is the unemployment rate that would result from the combination of economic, social, and political factors that exist at a time—assuming the economy was neither booming nor in recession. These forces include the usual pattern of companies expanding and contracting their workforces in a dynamic economy, social and economic forces that affect the labor market, or public policies that affect either the eagerness of people to work or the willingness of businesses to hire. Let’s discuss these factors in more detail.
p250.zh: 自然失业率并不是“自然”的,因为水在华氏32度时会冻结,在华氏212度时会沸腾。 它不是一个自然的物理和不变的法则。 相反,只有 " 自然 " 比率,因为当时存在的经济、社会和政治因素组合导致的失业率——假设经济既不繁荣,也不衰退。 这些力量包括公司在充满活力的经济中扩大和缩减劳动力的通常模式,影响劳动力市场的社会和经济力量,或影响人们工作热情或企业雇佣意愿的公共政策。 让我们更详细地讨论这些因素。

p252.original: In a market economy, some companies are always going broke for a variety of reasons: old technology; poor management; good management that happened to make bad decisions; shifts in tastes of consumers so that less of the firm’s product is desired; a large customer who went broke; or tough domestic or foreign competitors. Conversely, other companies will be doing very well for just the opposite reasons and looking to hire more employees. In a perfect world, all of those who lost jobs would immediately find new ones. However, in the real world, even if the number of job seekers is equal to the number of job vacancies, it takes time to find out about new jobs, to interview and figure out if the new job is a good match, or perhaps to sell a house and buy another in proximity to a new job. Economists call the unemployment that occurs in the meantime, as workers move between jobs, frictional unemployment. Frictional unemployment is not inherently a bad thing. It takes time on part of both the employer and the individual to match those looking for employment with the correct job openings. For individuals and companies to be successful and productive, you want people to find the job for which they are best suited, not just the first job offered.
p252.zh: 在市场经济中,一些公司总是因为各种原因破产:老技术;管理不善;管理良好,做出不好的决定;消费者的品味转变,从而减少对公司产品的需求;大客户破产;或国内或外国竞争对手强硬。反之,其他公司则会因为相反的原因表现得非常好,并寻求雇用更多的员工.在一个完美的世界里,所有失去工作的人都会立即找到新的工作。 然而,在现实世界中,即使求职者的数量与职位空缺的数量相等,也需要时间才能发现新的工作,面试和找出新工作是否匹配,或者也许可以卖房子,在靠近新工作的地方购买另一个.经济学家称这期间发生的失业,因为工人在工作间流动,摩擦性失业.摩擦性失业本质上并不是坏事。部分雇主和个人都需要时间,才能将寻找工作的人与正确的工作机会相匹配。 为了个人和公司取得成功和生产,你希望人们找到他们最适合的工作,而不仅仅是第一个提供的工作。

p253.original: In the mid-2000s, before the 2008–2009 recession, it was true that about 7% of U.S. workers saw their jobs disappear in any three-month period. However, in periods of economic growth, these destroyed jobs are counterbalanced for the economy as a whole by a larger number of jobs created. In 2019, for example, there were typically about 6 million unemployed people at any given time in the U.S. economy. Even though about two-thirds of those unemployed people found a job in 14 weeks or fewer, the unemployment rate did not change much during the year, because those who found new jobs were largely offset by others who lost jobs.
p253.zh: 在2000年代中期,在2008-2009年衰退之前,确实有约7%的美国工人看到他们在任何三个月的时间内消失。 然而,在经济增长的时期,这些被破坏的就业机会与创造的更多就业机会抵消了整个经济。 例如,2019年,美国经济中任何特定时间的失业人口一般有约600万. 尽管这些失业人员中有三分之二的人在14周或不到14周的时间里找到了工作,但失业率在这一年中并没有多大变化,因为找到新工作的人在很大程度上被其他失去工作的人所抵消。

p254.original: Of course, it would be preferable if people who were losing jobs could immediately and easily move into newly created jobs, but in the real world, that is not possible. Someone who is laid off by a textile mill in South Carolina cannot turn around and immediately start working for a textile mill in California. Instead, the adjustment process happens in ripples. Some people find new jobs near their old ones, while others find that they must move to new locations. Some people can do a very similar job with a different company, while others must start new career paths. Some people may be near retirement and decide to look only for part-time work, while others want an employer that offers a long-term career path. The frictional unemployment that results from people moving between jobs in a dynamic economy may account for one to two percentage points of total unemployment.
p254.zh: 当然,如果那些失去工作的人能够立即和容易地进入新创造的工作岗位,那将是可取的,但是在现实世界中,这是不可能的。被南卡罗来纳州一家纺织厂解雇的人不能转身,立即开始在加利福尼亚州一家纺织厂工作. 相反,调整过程发生在波折中.一些人在旧工作附近找到新的工作,而另一些人则发现他们必须搬到新的地点。 有些人可以在不同的公司做非常相似的工作,而其他人则必须开始新的职业道路.一些人可能接近退休,决定只寻找兼职工作,而另一些人则希望有一个提供长期职业道路的雇主. 在充满活力的经济中,人们在工作之间流动所产生的摩擦性失业可能占总失业的一至二个百分点。

p255.original: The level of frictional unemployment will depend on how easy it is for workers to learn about alternative jobs, which may reflect the ease of communications about job prospects in the economy. The extent of frictional unemployment will also depend to some extent on how willing people are to move to new areas to find jobs—which in turn may depend on history and culture.
p255.zh: 摩擦性失业水平将取决于工人了解替代工作有多容易,这可能反映关于经济中工作前景的交流比较容易。摩擦性失业的程度也在某种程度上取决于人们是否愿意移居到新的地区寻找工作,而就业又可能取决于历史和文化。

p256.original: Frictional unemployment and the natural rate of unemployment also seem to depend on the age distribution of the population.  (b) showed that unemployment rates are typically lower for people between 25–54 years of age or aged 55 and over than they are for those who are younger. “Prime-age workers,” as those in the 25–54 age bracket are sometimes called, are typically at a place in their lives when they want to have a job and income arriving at all times. In addition,  older workers who lose jobs may prefer to opt for retirement.  By contrast, it is likely that a relatively high proportion of those who are under 25 will be trying out jobs and life options, and this leads to greater job mobility and hence higher frictional unemployment. Thus, a society with a relatively high proportion of young workers, like the U.S. beginning in the mid-1960s when Baby Boomers began entering the labor market, will tend to have a higher unemployment rate than a society with a higher proportion of its workers in older ages.
p256.zh: 急速失业和自然失业率似乎也取决于人口的年龄分布。(b) 表明25至54岁或55岁及以上者的失业率通常低于较年轻者。25-54岁年龄段的 " 小学工人 " 有时被称作 " 小学工人 " ,他们通常在其生活的一个地方,当他们想要随时得到工作和收入时。 此外,失去工作的老年工人可能更愿意选择退休。相比之下,25岁以下的人中很可能有相当大比例的人会尝试工作和生活选择,这会导致更大的工作流动性,从而增加摩擦性失业。 因此,一个年轻工人比例相对较高的社会,如1960年代中期开始的美国,即Baby Boomers开始进入劳动力市场时,其失业率往往比老年工人比例较高的社会要高。

p258.original: Another factor that influences the natural rate of unemployment is the amount of structural unemployment. The structurally unemployed are individuals who have no jobs because they lack skills valued by the labor market, either because demand has shifted away from the skills they do have, or because they never learned any skills. An example of the former would be the unemployment among aerospace engineers after the U.S. space program downsized in the 1970s. An example of the latter would be high school dropouts.
p258.zh: 影响自然失业率的另一个因素是结构性失业率。结构失业的人是没有工作的人,因为他们缺乏劳动力市场所重视的技能,或者是因为需求已经偏离了他们拥有的技能,或者因为他们从未学到任何技能。前者的一个例子是美国空间方案在1970年代缩小后航空航天工程师的失业率。后者的一个例子是高中辍学。

p259.original: Some people worry that technology causes structural unemployment. In the past, new technologies have put lower skilled employees out of work, but at the same time they create demand for higher skilled workers to use the new technologies. Education seems to be the key in minimizing the amount of structural unemployment. Individuals who have degrees can be retrained if they become structurally unemployed. For people with no skills and little education, that option is more limited.
p259.zh: 一些人担心技术会造成结构性失业. 过去,新技术使技术水平较低的雇员失业,但与此同时,新技术又对技术水平较高的工人产生了使用新技术的需求。教育似乎是尽量减少结构性失业的关键。 有学位的个人如果在结构上失业,可以重新接受培训。 对于没有技能和受教育程度低的人来说,这种选择是比较有限的。

p260.original: Natural Unemployment and Potential Real GDP
p260.zh: 自然失业和潜在实际国内生产总值

p261.original: The natural unemployment rate is related to two other important concepts: full employment and potential real GDP. Economists consider the economy to be at full employment when the actual unemployment rate is equal to the natural unemployment rate. When the economy is at full employment, real GDP is equal to potential real GDP.  By contrast, when the economy is below full employment, the unemployment rate is greater than the natural unemployment rate and real GDP is less than potential. Finally, when the economy is above full employment, then the unemployment rate is less than the natural unemployment rate and real GDP is greater than potential. Operating above potential is only possible for a short while, since it is analogous to all workers working overtime.
p261.zh: 自然失业率与另外两个重要概念有关:充分就业和潜在的实际国内生产总值。经济学家认为,当实际失业率与自然失业率相等时,经济处于充分就业状态. 当经济实现充分就业时,实际GDP等于潜在的实际GDP.相比之下,当经济低于充分就业时,失业率高于自然失业率,实际国内生产总值低于潜力。 最后,当经济高于充分就业时,失业率低于自然失业率,实际国内生产总值大于潜力。超潜力操作只能短时间进行,因为它类似于所有加班工人。

p262.original: Productivity Shifts and the Natural Rate of Unemployment
p262.zh: 生产力变化和自然失业率

p263.original: Unexpected shifts in productivity can have a powerful effect on the natural rate of unemployment. Over time, workers' productivity determines the level of wages in an economy. After all, if a business paid workers more than could be justified by their productivity, the business will ultimately lose money and go bankrupt. Conversely, if a business tries to pay workers less than their productivity then, in a competitive labor market, other businesses will find it worthwhile to hire away those workers and pay them more.
p263.zh: 生产力的意外变化会对自然失业率产生有力影响。随着时间的推移,工人的生产力决定着经济中的工资水平.毕竟,如果一个企业的工人的工资比他们的生产力更合理,那么这个企业最终会失去钱财,破产. 相反,如果一个企业试图向工人支付低于其生产率的报酬,那么,在竞争性的劳动力市场上,其他企业会发现有必要雇用这些工人,并给他们更多的报酬。

p264.original: However, adjustments of wages to productivity levels will not happen quickly or smoothly. Employers typically review wages only once or twice a year. In many modern jobs, it is difficult to measure productivity at the individual level. For example, how precisely would one measure the quantity produced by an accountant who is one of many people working in the tax department of a large corporation? Because productivity is difficult to observe, employers often determine wage increases based on recent experience with productivity. If productivity has been rising at, say, 2% per year, then wages rise at that level as well. However, when productivity changes unexpectedly, it can affect the natural rate of unemployment for a time.
p264.zh: 然而,工资与生产力水平的调整不会迅速或顺利进行。雇主通常每年只审查一次或两次工资。在许多现代工作方面,很难在个人一级衡量生产率。 例如,对于在大公司税务部门工作的许多人之一的会计师所生产的数量,人们将如何精确地加以衡量? 由于生产率难以观察,雇主往往根据近期的生产率经验决定工资的提高。 如果生产率一直以每年2%的速度增长,那么工资水平也会上升。 然而,当生产力发生意想不到的变化时,它可能会在一段时间内影响自然失业率.

p265.original: The U.S. economy in the 1970s and 1990s provides two vivid examples of this process. In the 1970s, productivity growth slowed down unexpectedly (as we discussed in Economic Growth). For example, output per hour of U.S. workers in the business sector increased at an annual rate of 3.3% per year from 1960 to 1973, but only 0.8% from 1973 to 1982.  (a) illustrates the situation where the demand for labor—that is, the quantity of labor that business is willing to hire at any given wage—has been shifting out a little each year because of rising productivity, from D0 to D1 to D2. As a result, equilibrium wages have been rising each year from W0 to W1 to W2. However, when productivity unexpectedly slows down, the pattern of wage increases does not adjust right away. Wages keep rising each year from W2 to W3 to W4, but the demand for labor is no longer shifting up. A gap opens where the quantity of labor supplied at wage level W4 is greater than the quantity demanded. The natural rate of unemployment rises. In the aftermath of this unexpectedly low productivity in the 1970s, the national unemployment rate did not fall below 7% from May, 1980 until 1986. Over time, the rise in wages will adjust to match the slower gains in productivity, and the unemployment rate will ease back down, but this process may take years.
p265.zh: 1970年代和1990年代的美国经济为这一进程提供了两个生动的例子. 在1970年代,生产率增长意外放缓(我们在《经济增长》中曾讨论过这一点)。 例如,美国商业部门工人的每小时产出从1960年到1973年以每年3.3%的速度增长,但从1973年到1982年只有0.8%.(a) 说明由于生产率的提高,对劳动力的需求——即企业愿意以任何特定工资雇用的劳动力数量——每年略有减少,从D0到D1到D2。 因此,平衡工资每年从W0增长到W1增长到W2. 然而,当生产力出人意料地放慢时,工资增长的规律不会立即调整.工资每年从W2增长到W3增长到W4,但劳动力需求不再上升。 在W4级劳动力数量大于所需数量的情况下,差距就会拉开。自然失业率上升。 在1970年代生产力出人意料的低下之后,从1980年5月到1986年,全国失业率并没有下降到7%以下。随着时间的推移,工资的上涨将进行调整,以适应生产力增长较慢的情况,失业率将回落,但这一过程可能需要数年时间。

p266.zh: 非预期的生产力变化和失业

p267.original: The late 1990s provide an opposite example: instead of the surprise decline in productivity that occurred in the 1970s, productivity unexpectedly rose in the mid-1990s. The annual growth rate of real output per hour of labor increased from 1.7% from 1980–1995, to an annual rate of 2.6% from 1995–2001. Let’s simplify the situation a bit, so that the economic lesson of the story is easier to see graphically, and say that productivity had not been increasing at all in earlier years, so the intersection of the labor market was at point E in  (b), where the demand curve for labor (D0) intersects the supply curve for labor. As a result, real wages were not increasing. Now, productivity jumps upward, which shifts the demand for labor out to the right, from D0 to D1. At least for a time, however, wages are still set according to the earlier expectations of no productivity growth, so wages do not rise. The result is that at the prevailing wage level (W), the quantity of labor demanded (Qd) will for a time exceed the quantity of labor supplied (Qs), and unemployment will be very low—actually below the natural level of unemployment for a time. This pattern of unexpectedly high productivity helps to explain why the unemployment rate stayed below 4.5%—quite a low level by historical standards—from 1998 until after the U.S. economy had entered a recession in 2001.
p267.zh: 1990年代后期提供了一个相反的例子:与1970年代生产力的突然下降相反,1990年代中期生产力出乎意料地上升。劳动力每小时实际产出的年增长率从1980-1995年的1.7%增加到1995-2001年的2.6%。 让我们简单一点,这样故事的经济教训就更容易用图形来理解,并说生产力在前几年根本没有增长,因此劳动力市场的交汇点在(b)的E点,即劳动力的需求曲线(D0)与劳动力的供应曲线交叉。 因此,实际工资没有增加。 现在,生产率上升,这把劳动力需求从D0向右转移,从D0到D1。 然而,至少一段时间以来,工资仍然按照早先的预期,即不提高生产率,因此工资不会上升。结果是,在现行工资水平(W)下,一段时间内所需劳动力(Qd)将超过所提供的劳动力(Qs),失业率将非常低,实际上一度低于自然失业率。 这种出乎意料的高生产率模式有助于解释为什么失业率一直低于历史标准4.5-

p268.original: Levels of unemployment will tend to be somewhat higher on average when productivity is unexpectedly low, and conversely, will tend to be somewhat lower on average when productivity is unexpectedly high. However, over time, wages do eventually adjust to reflect productivity levels.
p268.zh: 如果生产力出乎意料地低,平均失业率往往会略高一些,反之,如果生产力出乎意料地高,平均失业率往往会略低一些。 然而,随着时间的推移,工资确实最终作了调整,以反映生产力水平。

p269.original: Public Policy and the Natural Rate of Unemployment
p269.zh: 公共政策和自然失业率

p270.original: Public policy can also have a powerful effect on the natural rate of unemployment. On the supply side of the labor market, public policies to assist the unemployed can affect how eager people are to find work. For example, if a worker who loses a job is guaranteed a generous package of unemployment insurance, welfare benefits, food stamps, and government medical benefits, then the opportunity cost of unemployment is lower and that worker will be less eager to seek a new job.
p270.zh: 公共政策还可以对自然失业率产生强有力的影响。 在劳动力市场的供应方面,帮助失业者的公共政策会影响人们寻找工作的迫切性。 例如,如果失去工作的工人得到一揽子慷慨的失业保险、福利、粮票和政府医疗福利的保障,那么失业的机会成本就会降低,而工人对寻找新工作的热心也会降低。

p271.original: What seems to matter most is not just the amount of these benefits, but how long they last. A society that provides generous help for the unemployed that cuts off after, say, six months, may provide less of an incentive for unemployment than a society that provides less generous help that lasts for several years. Conversely, government assistance for job search or retraining can in some cases encourage people back to work sooner. See the Clear it Up to learn how the U.S. handles unemployment insurance.
p271.zh: 似乎最重要的不仅仅是这些福利的数量,而是这些福利持续多久。向失业人员提供慷慨帮助的社会,在六个月后中断工作,可能比向失业提供慷慨帮助的社会提供失业奖励要少。 相反,政府协助寻找工作或再培训在某些情况下可以鼓励人们更早地返回工作岗位。 见The Clear It Up来学习美国如何处理失业保险.

p272.original: How does U.S. unemployment insurance work?
p272.zh: 美国失业保险如何运作?.

p273.original: Unemployment insurance is a joint federal–state program that the federal government enacted in 1935. While the federal government sets minimum standards for the program, state governments conduct most of the administration.
p273.zh: 失业保险是联邦政府于1935年颁布的联邦-州联合方案. 虽然联邦政府为该方案规定了最低标准,但州政府则负责大部分行政工作。

p274.original: The funding for the program is a federal tax collected from employers. The federal government requires tax collection on the first $7,000 in wages paid to each worker; however, states can choose to collect the tax on a higher amount if they wish, and 41 states have set a higher limit. States can choose the length of time that they pay benefits, although most states limit unemployment benefits to 26 weeks—with extensions possible in times of especially high unemployment. The states then use the fund to pay benefits to those who become unemployed. Average unemployment benefits are equal to about one-third of the wage that the person earned in their previous job, but the level of unemployment benefits varies considerably across states.
p274.zh: 该方案的资金是向雇主征收的联邦税。联邦政府要求向每个工人支付的工资前七千元的税收;然而,各州如果愿意,可以选择更高额的税收,41个州规定了更高的限额.国家可以选择支付福利的时间长度,尽管大多数州将失业福利限制在26周之内——在失业率特别高的情况下,可以延长。各州然后利用该基金向失业人员支付福利。平均失业福利相当于此人在以前工作期间挣得的工资的三分之一左右,但各州失业福利水平差别很大。

p276.original: Bottom 10 States That Pay the Lowest Benefit per Week
p276.zh: 每星期支付最低养恤金的10个最低国家

p277.original: Top 10 States That Pay the Highest Benefit per Week
p277.zh: 每星期支付最高福利的前10个国家

p318.original: One other interesting thing to note about the classifications of unemployment—an individual does not have to collect unemployment benefits to be classified as unemployed. While there are statistics kept and studied relating to how many people are collecting unemployment insurance, this is not the source of unemployment rate information.
p318.zh: 关于失业的分类,还有一件有趣的事情需要注意——一个人不必领取失业津贴而要归类为失业。 虽然有关于有多少人领取失业保险的统计数字得到保存和研究,但这不是失业率信息的来源。

p319.original: View this  article  for an explanation of exactly who is eligible for unemployment benefits.
p319.zh: 查看这一条是为了解释究竟谁有资格领取失业津贴。

p320.original: On the demand side of the labor market, government rules, social institutions, and the presence of unions can affect the willingness of firms to hire. For example, if a government makes it hard for businesses to start up or to expand, by wrapping new businesses in bureaucratic red tape, then businesses will become more discouraged about hiring. Government regulations can make it harder to start a business by requiring that a new business obtain many permits and pay many fees, or by restricting the types and quality of products that a company can sell. Other government regulations, like zoning laws, may limit where companies can conduct business, or whether businesses are allowed to be open during evenings or on Sunday.
p320.zh: 在劳动力市场的需求方面,政府规则、社会机构以及工会的存在会影响企业的雇用意愿。 例如,如果政府让企业难以开办或扩大,通过将新的企业包装在官僚主义的繁文缛节中,那么企业就会更加不愿意雇用员工. 政府规章可以要求新企业获得许多许可证并支付许多费用,或者限制公司可以销售的产品的类型和质量,从而使创业变得更加困难。 其他政府规章,如分区法,可能会限制公司可以做生意的地方,或者是否允许企业在晚上或星期日营业.

p321.original: Whatever rationales may be offered for such laws in terms of social value—like the value some Muslim people place on not working on Friday, or some Jewish people on not working on Saturday, or some Christian people on not working on Sunday—these kinds of restrictions create a difference between some willing workers and other willing employers, and thus contribute to a higher natural rate of unemployment. Similarly, if government makes it difficult to fire or lay off workers, businesses may react by trying not to hire more workers than strictly necessary—since laying these workers off would be costly and difficult. High minimum wages may discourage businesses from hiring low-skill workers. Government rules may encourage and support powerful unions, which can then push up wages for union workers, but at a cost of discouraging businesses from hiring those workers.
p321.zh: 不论这些法律在社会价值方面有何理由,例如某些穆斯林人认为星期五不工作,或某些犹太人认为星期六不工作,或一些基督教人认为星期天不工作,这些限制造成了一些愿意工作的工人和其他愿意工作的雇主之间的差别,从而导致较高的自然失业率。 同样,如果政府使解雇或解雇工人变得困难,企业可能会作出反应,试图不雇用比绝对必要的更多的工人,因为解雇这些工人将既昂贵又困难。高最低工资可能阻碍企业雇用低技能工人。 政府规则可以鼓励和支持强大的工会,工会随后可以提高工会工人的工资,但代价是劝阻企业雇用这些工人。

p322.original: The Natural Rate of Unemployment in Recent Years

p323.original: The underlying economic, social, and political factors that determine the natural rate of unemployment can change over time, which means that the natural rate of unemployment can change over time, too.
p323.zh: 确定自然失业率的基本经济、社会和政治因素会随时间而变化,这意味着自然失业率也会随时间而变化。

p324.original:
Estimates by economists of the natural rate of unemployment in the U.S. economy in the early 2000s run at about 4.5 to 5.5%. This is a lower estimate than earlier. We outline three of the common reasons that economists propose for this change below.
        The internet has provided a remarkable new tool through which job seekers can find out about jobs at different companies and can make contact with relative ease. An internet search is far easier than trying to find a list of local employers and then hunting up phone numbers for all of their human resources departments, and requesting a list of jobs and application forms. Social networking sites such as LinkedIn have changed how people find work as well.
The growth of the temporary worker industry has probably helped to reduce the natural rate of unemployment. In the early 1980s, only about 0.5% of all workers held jobs through temp agencies. By the early 2000s, the figure had risen above 2%. Temp agencies can provide jobs for workers while they are looking for permanent work. They can also serve as a clearinghouse, helping workers find out about jobs with certain employers and getting a tryout with the employer. For many workers, a temp job is a stepping-stone to a permanent job that they might not have heard about or obtained any other way, so the growth of temp jobs will also tend to reduce frictional unemployment.
The aging of the “baby boom generation”—the especially large generation of Americans born between 1946 and 1964—meant that the proportion of young workers in the economy was relatively high in the 1970s, as the boomers entered the labor market, but is relatively low today. As we noted earlier, middle-aged and older workers are far more likely to experience low unemployment than younger workers, a factor that tends to reduce the natural rate of unemployment as the baby boomers age.
p324.zh: 经济学家对2000年代初期美国经济的自然失业率的估计约为4.5%至5.5%。 这比早先的估计数要低。 我们概述了经济学家为这一改变提出的三个共同理由。互联网提供了一个引人注目的新工具,求职者可以通过这一工具了解不同公司的工作情况,并能相对容易地进行接触。网路搜索远比寻找当地雇主名单、寻找所有人力资源部门的电话号码、索取工作清单和申请表容易得多。LinkedIn等社交网站也改变了人们找到工作的方式。临时工人行业的增长可能有助于降低自然失业率。 在1980年代初,只有大约0.5%的工人通过临时机构工作。 到2000年代初期,这一数字已上升至2%以上。临时机构可以在工人寻找长期工作时为他们提供工作。 他们也可以充当一个信息中心,帮助工人了解与某些雇主的工作情况,并与雇主进行试训。 对于许多工人来说,临时工作是他们可能没有听说或没有获得任何其他方式的永久工作的跳板,因此临时工作的增长也往往会减少摩擦性失业." 婴儿潮一代 " -- -- 1946年至1964年间出生的一代美国人人数特别多 -- -- 的老龄化表明,随着繁荣者进入劳动力市场,青年工人在经济中的比例在1970年代相对较高,但今天却相对较低。 正如我们早些时候指出的,中年和老年工人的失业率比年轻工人低得多,随着婴儿生长者年龄的增长,这一因素往往会降低自然失业率。

p325.original: The combined result of these factors is that the natural rate of unemployment was on average lower in the 1990s and the early 2000s than in the 1980s. The 2008–2009 Great Recession pushed monthly unemployment rates up to 10% in late 2009. However, even at that time, the Congressional Budget Office was forecasting that by 2015, unemployment rates would fall back to about 5%. During the first two months of 2020, the unemployment rate held steady at 3.5%. As of the first quarter of 2022, the Congressional Budget Office estimates the natural rate to be 4.6%.
p325.zh: 这些因素的综合结果是,1990年代和2000年代初期的自然失业率平均低于1980年代。2008-2009年大衰退将每月失业率推至2009年底的10%。 然而,即使在那时,国会预算办公室也在预测,到2015年,失业率将回落到5%左右. 在2020年前两个月,失业率稳定在3.5%。 截至2022年第一季度,国会预算办公室估计自然比率为4.6%.

p326.original: The Natural Rate of Unemployment in Europe

p327.original: By the standards of other high-income economies, the natural rate of unemployment in the U.S. economy appears relatively low. Through good economic years and bad, many European economies have had unemployment rates hovering near 10%, or even higher, since the 1970s. European rates of unemployment have been higher not because recessions in Europe have been deeper, but rather because the conditions underlying supply and demand for labor have been different in Europe, in a way that has created a much higher natural rate of unemployment.
p327.zh: 根据其他高收入经济体的标准,美国经济的自然失业率似乎相对较低.20世纪70年代以来,许多欧洲经济体通过良好的经济年限和糟糕的年限,失业率徘徊在10%左右,甚至更高。 欧洲失业率较高,不是因为欧洲经济衰退更深,而是因为欧洲劳动力供求条件不同,造成高得多的自然失业率。

p328.original: Many European countries have a combination of generous welfare and unemployment benefits, together with nests of rules that impose additional costs on businesses when they hire. In addition, many countries have laws that require firms to give workers months of notice before laying them off and to provide substantial severance or retraining packages after laying them off. The legally required notice before laying off a worker can be more than three months in Spain, Germany, Denmark, and Belgium, and the legally required severance package can be as high as a year’s salary or more in Austria, Spain, Portugal, Italy, and Greece. Such laws will surely discourage laying off or firing current workers. However, when companies know that it will be difficult to fire or lay off workers, they also become hesitant about hiring in the first place.
p328.zh: 许多欧洲国家同时提供慷慨的福利和失业福利,同时制定许多规则,在雇用企业时给企业带来额外的成本。 此外,许多国家的法律要求公司在解雇工人之前提前几个月通知工人,并在解雇工人后提供大量离职或再培训。 在西班牙、德国、丹麦和比利时,法律要求解雇工人前的通告可能超过三个月,而在奥地利、西班牙、葡萄牙、意大利和希腊,法律要求的解雇计划可能与一年或一年以上的工资一样高。这些法律肯定会阻止解雇或解雇现有工人。 然而,当公司知道很难解雇或解雇工人时,它们也开始对雇用感到犹豫。

p329.original: We can attribute the typically higher levels of unemployment in many European countries in recent years, which have prevailed even when economies are growing at a solid pace, to the fact that the sorts of laws and regulations that lead to a high natural rate of unemployment are much more prevalent in Europe than in the United States.
p329.zh: 最近几年,许多欧洲国家的失业率通常较高,即使在经济稳步增长的情况下,失业率也仍然很高,我们可以将这种情况归因于导致高自然失业率的法律和规章在欧洲比在美国普遍得多。

p330.original: A Preview of Policies to Fight Unemployment

p331.original: The Government Budgets and Fiscal Policy and Macroeconomic Policy Around the World chapters provide a detailed discussion of how to fight unemployment, when we can discuss these policies in the context of the full array of macroeconomic goals and frameworks for analysis. However, even at this preliminary stage, it is useful to preview the main issues concerning policies to fight unemployment.
p331.zh: 《政府预算和财政政策》和《宏观经济政策环绕世界》各章详细讨论了如何解决失业问题,届时我们可以在一整套宏观经济目标和分析框架的范围内讨论这些政策。 然而,即使在这一初步阶段,也有必要对与消除失业政策有关的主要问题进行探讨。

p332.original:
The remedy for unemployment will depend on the diagnosis. Cyclical unemployment is a short-term problem, caused because the economy is in a recession. Thus, the preferred solution will be to avoid or minimize recessions. As Government Budgets and Fiscal Policy
   discusses, governments can enact this policy by stimulating the overall buying power in the economy, so that firms perceive that sales and profits are possible, which makes them eager to hire.
p332.zh: 失业的补救办法将取决于诊断结果。循环失业是一个短期问题,因为经济处于衰退之中。 因此,首选解决办法将是避免或尽量减少衰退。 正如政府预算和财政政策所讨论的那样,政府可以通过刺激经济的总体购买力来颁布这项政策,从而使公司认识到销售和利润是可能的,从而使它们渴望雇用。

p333.original: Dealing with the natural rate of unemployment is trickier. In a market-oriented economy, firms will hire and fire workers. Governments cannot control this. Furthermore, the evolving age structure of the economy's population, or unexpected shifts in productivity are beyond a government's control and, will affect the natural rate of unemployment for a time. However, as the example of high ongoing unemployment rates for many European countries illustrates, government policy clearly can affect the natural rate of unemployment that will persist even when GDP is growing.
p333.zh: 处理自然失业率比较狡猾。 在市场经济中,公司将雇用和解雇工人。 政府不能控制这种情况。 此外,经济人口年龄结构的变化,或生产力的意外变化,超出了政府的控制范围,将影响一段时间的自然失业率。 然而,正如许多欧洲国家持续高失业率的例子所显示的,政府政策显然会影响到即使在国内生产总值增长时仍将持续存在的自然失业率。

p334.original: When a government enacts policies that will affect workers or employers, it must examine how these policies will affect the information and incentives employees and employers have to find one another. For example, the government may have a role to play in helping some of the unemployed with job searches. Governments may need to rethink the design of their programs that offer assistance to unemployed workers and protections to employed workers so that they will not unduly discourage the supply of labor. Similarly, governments may need to reassess rules that make it difficult for businesses to begin or to expand so that they will not unduly discourage the demand for labor. The message is not that governments should repeal all laws affecting labor markets, but only that when they enact such laws, a society that cares about unemployment will need to consider the tradeoffs involved.
p334.zh: 当政府颁布影响工人或雇主的政策时,它必须审查这些政策将如何影响雇员和雇主之间必须找到的信息和激励措施。 例如,政府在帮助一些失业者寻找工作方面可能发挥作用。 政府可能需要重新考虑其向失业工人提供援助和向就业工人提供保护的方案的设计,以便他们不会不适当地阻止劳动力的供应。 同样,政府可能需要重新评估那些使企业难以开始或扩大的规则,以便它们不会不适当地抑制对劳动力的需求。信息并不是政府应该废除所有影响劳动力市场的法律,而只是当政府颁布此类法律时,一个关心失业问题的社会需要考虑所涉及的权衡。

p336.original: Almost two years after the pandemic began, the unemployment rate was on track to go below 4% again by early- to mid-2022. While this is great news for workers, we have also seen that the story of the labor market is more complicated than a single statistic might suggest. Millions remained out of the labor force due to the public health situation, and the percentage of workers unemployed for longer than 26 weeks was still high.
p336.zh: 这场流行病爆发近两年后,失业率有望在2022年初至中期再次低于4%。 虽然这对工人来说是一个好消息,但我们也看到,劳动力市场的故事比单一统计数据可能表明的更加复杂。 由于公共卫生状况,数百万人仍然处于劳动力之外,超过26周的工人失业比例仍然很高。

p337.original: The shift to remote work helped the unemployment rate come down by providing greater flexibility for workers concerned with their health and safety. But it didn't help workers, especially women, who continued to be burdened with excessive care responsibilities at home. During 2020, the unemployment rate for women exceeded that of men by over a full percentage point. Additionally, virus variants in other countries threatened to disrupt progress made at home and abroad.
p337.zh: 转向远程工作有助于降低失业率,为关心其健康和安全的工人提供更大的灵活性。 但是这并没有帮助工人,特别是妇女,她们继续承担着在家中过度的照料责任.2020年,妇女失业率超过男性,超过了男性的完整百分点. 此外,其他国家的病毒变种有可能破坏国内外取得的进展。

p338.original: The pandemic has helped shed light on how we can use information from all areas of the labor market to evaluate the health of the economy.
p338.zh: 这一大流行病有助于阐明我们如何利用劳动力市场所有领域的信息评估经济健康状况。

p340.original: The natural rate of unemployment is the rate of unemployment that the economic, social, and political forces in the economy would cause even when the economy is not in a recession. These factors include the frictional unemployment that occurs when people either choose to change jobs or are put out of work for a time by the shifts of a dynamic and changing economy. They also include any laws concerning conditions of hiring and firing that have the undesired side effect of discouraging job formation. They also include structural unemployment, which occurs when demand shifts permanently away from a certain type of job skill.
p340.zh: 自然失业率是经济、社会和政治力量即使在经济没有衰退的情况下也会造成的失业率。这些因素包括:当人们选择改变工作,或者由于充满活力和不断变化的经济的转变而暂时失业时,就出现了摩擦性失业。这些法律还包括关于雇用和解雇条件的任何法律,这些法律具有阻碍就业的不良副作用。这些问题还包括结构性失业,这种失业是在需求永久脱离某一类工作技能时发生的。

p342.original: Is the increase in labor force participation rates among women better thought of as causing an increase in cyclical unemployment or an increase in the natural rate of unemployment? Why?
p342.zh: 妇女劳动力参与率的提高是否更能引起周期性失业的增加或自然失业率的上升? 为什么?

p343.original: The increase in labor supply was a social demographic trend—it was not caused by the economy falling into a recession. Therefore, the influx of women into the work force increased the natural rate of unemployment.
p343.zh: 劳动力供应的增加是一个社会人口趋势——这不是经济陷入衰退造成的。 因此,妇女进入劳动力队伍增加了自然失业率。

p344.original: Many college students graduate from college before they have found a job. When graduates begin to look for a job, they are counted as what category of unemployed?
p344.zh: 许多大学生在找到工作之前就从大学毕业. 当毕业生开始寻找工作时,他们被算作是哪一类失业?

p345.original: New entrants to the labor force, whether from college or otherwise, are counted as frictionally unemployed until they find a job.
p345.zh: 无论是从大学还是从其他角度来说,新加入劳动力队伍的人在找到工作之前,都被视为摩擦性失业。

p347.original: What term describes the remaining level of unemployment that occurs even when the economy is healthy?
p347.zh: 哪种术语描述即使在经济健康的情况下仍然会出现的失业率?

p348.original: What forces create the natural rate of unemployment for an economy?
p348.zh: 是什么因素造成一个经济体的自然失业率?

p349.original: Would you expect the natural rate of unemployment to be roughly the same in different countries?
p349.zh: 你会期望不同国家的自然失业率大致相同吗?

p350.original: Would you expect the natural rate of unemployment to remain the same within one country over the long run of several decades?
p350.zh: 你是否期望一个国家的自然失业率在数十年中保持不变?

p351.original: What is frictional unemployment? Give examples of frictional unemployment.
p351.zh: 什么是摩擦性失业? 请举出摩擦性失业的例子。

p352.original: What is structural unemployment? Give examples of structural unemployment.
p352.zh: 什么是结构性失业?举结构性失业的例子。

p353.original: After several years of economic growth, would you expect the unemployment in an economy to be mainly cyclical or mainly due to the natural rate of unemployment? Why?
p353.zh: 经过几年的经济增长后,你是否期望一个经济体的失业率主要是周期性或主要由于自然失业率? 为什么?

p354.original:
What type of unemployment (cyclical, frictional, or
  structural) applies to each of the following:
  landscapers laid off in response to a drop in new
  housing construction during a recession.
coal miners laid off due to EPA regulations that
  shut down coal fired power
a financial analyst who quits his/her job in
  Chicago and is pursing similar work in Arizonaprinters laid off due to drop in demand for
  printed catalogues and flyers as firms go the
  internet to promote an advertise their products.
factory workers in the U.S. laid off as the plants shut down and move to Mexico and Ireland.
p354.zh: 哪种类型的失业(周期性、摩擦性或结构性的)适用于以下每一种情况:在衰退期间,由于新住房建设的下降,地貌景观者被解雇。 煤矿工人由于环保局的条例而被解雇,关闭了煤电,而金融分析员则辞去了在芝加哥的工作,在亚利桑那州印刷工人也从事类似的工作,因为公司上互联网宣传其产品时,对印刷品目录和传单的需求下降。 美国的工厂工人由于工厂关闭并迁往墨西哥和爱尔兰而被解雇。

p356.original: Under what condition would a decrease in unemployment be bad for the economy?
p356.zh: 在什么条件下,降低失业率对经济不利?

p357.original: Under what condition would an increase in the unemployment rate be a positive sign?
p357.zh: 在什么条件下,提高失业率是一个积极的迹象?

p358.original: As the baby boom generation retires, the ratio of retirees to workers will increase noticeably. How will this affect the Social Security program? How will this affect the standard of living of the average American?
p358.zh: 随着婴儿潮一代退休,退休人员与工人的比例将明显增加。 这会对社会保障方案产生何种影响?这会如何影响美国普通人的生活水平?

p359.original: Unemployment rates have been higher in many European countries in recent decades than in the United States. Is the main reason for this long-term difference in unemployment rates more likely to be cyclical unemployment or the natural rate of unemployment? Explain briefly.
p359.zh: 近几十年来,许多欧洲国家的失业率一直高于美国。失业率长期差异的主要原因是否更可能是周期性失业或自然失业率?简单解释一下

p360.original: Is it desirable to pursue a goal of zero unemployment? Why or why not?
p360.zh: 是否应该追求零失业的目标? 为什么或为什么不呢?

p361.original: Is it desirable to eliminate natural unemployment? Why or why not? Hint: Think about what our economy would look like today and what assumptions would have to be met to have a zero rate of natural unemployment.
p361.zh: 消除自然失业是否可取? 为什么或为什么不呢?提示:考虑一下我们的经济今天会是什么样子,需要满足什么假设才能有零的自然失业率.

p362.original: The U.S. unemployment rate increased from 4.6% in July 2001 to 5.9% by June 2002. Without studying the subject in any detail, would you expect that a change of this kind is more likely to be due to cyclical unemployment or a change in the natural rate of unemployment? Why?
p362.zh: 美国的失业率从2001年7月的4.6%上升到2002年6月的5.9%。 如果不详细研究这个课题,你是否期望这种变化更可能是由于周期性失业或自然失业率的变化? 为什么?

p364.original: As the baby boomer generation retires, what should happen to wages and employment? Can you show this graphically?
p364.zh: 随着婴儿潮一代的退休,工资和就业应该怎么样? 你能用图形来显示吗?

c3.original: The U.S. unemployment rate moves up and down as the economy moves in and out of recessions. However, over time, the unemployment rate seems to return to a range of 4% to 6%. There does not seem to be a long-term trend toward the rate moving generally higher or generally lower. (Source: Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED), Unemployment Rate (UNRATE), https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/UNRATE)
c3.zh: 随着经济衰退的发生,美国的失业率不断上升和下降。 然而,随着时间的推移,失业率似乎又回到4%至6%之间。似乎没有长期的趋势,即利率普遍上升或普遍下降。(资料来源:联邦储备经济数据,失业率,https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/UNRATE)

c4.original: (a) By gender, 1948–2020. Unemployment rates for men used to be lower than unemployment rates for women, but in recent decades, the two rates have been very close, often– and especially during and soon after the Great Recession –  with the unemployment rate for men somewhat higher. (b) By age, 1948–2020. Unemployment rates are highest for the very young and become lower with age. (c) By race and ethnicity, 1974–2020. Although unemployment rates for all groups tend to rise and fall together, the unemployment rate for Black people is typically about twice as high as that for White people, while the unemployment rate for Hispanic people is in between. (Source: www.bls.gov)
c4.zh: (a) 按性别分列,1948-2020年。男性的失业率曾经低于女性失业率,但近几十年来,这两种失业率非常接近,特别是在大衰退期间和之后不久,男性失业率略高。(b) 按年龄分列,1948-2020年。青年失业率最高,随着年龄的增长而降低。(c) 按种族和族裔划分,1974-2020年。 虽然所有群体的失业率都趋于上升和下降,但黑人的失业率一般是白人的两倍左右,而西班牙裔人的失业率介于两者之间。(资料来源:www.bls.gov)

c5.original: In a labor market with flexible wages, the equilibrium will occur at wage We and quantity Qe, where the number of people who want jobs (shown by S) equals the number of jobs available (shown by D).
c5.zh: 在一个工资灵活的劳动力市场中,平衡将发生在工资和Qe数量上,其中需要工作的人数(由S来决定)相当于可获得的工作数量(由D来决定)。

c6.original: Because the wage rate is stuck at W, above the equilibrium, the number of those who want jobs (Qs) is greater than the number of job openings (Qd). The result is unemployment, shown by the bracket in the figure.
c6.zh: 由于工资率停留在W,高于平衡,因此需要工作(Qs)的人数大于职位空缺(Qd).结果是失业,以数字中的括号表示。

c7.original: (a) In a labor market where wages are able to rise, an increase in the demand for labor from D0 to D1 leads to an increase in equilibrium quantity of labor hired from Q0 to Q1 and a rise in the equilibrium wage from W0 to W1. (b) In a labor market where wages do not decline, a fall in the demand for labor from D0 to D1 leads to a decline in the quantity of labor demanded at the original wage (W0) from Q0 to Q2. These workers will want to work at the prevailing wage (W0), but will not be able to find jobs.
c7.zh: (a) 在工资能够上升的劳动力市场,对劳动力的需求从D0增长到D1,导致所雇用劳动力的平衡数量从Q0增长到Q1,平衡工资从W0增长到W1。(b) 在一个工资不下降的劳动力市场,对劳动力的需求从D0降至D1,导致按原工资(W0)要求的劳动力数量从Q0降至Q2。 这些工人希望按现行工资(W0)工作,但找不到工作。

c8.original: (a) Productivity is rising, increasing the demand for labor. Employers and workers become used to the pattern of wage increases. Then productivity suddenly stops increasing. However, there is a delay or lag in the recognition that productivity is no longer increasing. As a result, wages keep rising as before, but the demand for labor is no longer increasing, so at wage W3 and wage W4, unemployment exists where the quantity supplied of labor exceeds the quantity demanded. (b) The rate of productivity increase has been zero for a time, so employers and workers have come to accept the equilibrium wage level (W). Then productivity increases unexpectedly, shifting demand for labor from D0 to D1. At the wage (W), this means that the quantity demanded of labor exceeds the quantity supplied, and with job offers plentiful, the unemployment rate will be low.
c8.zh: (a) 生产力不断提高,增加了对劳动力的需求。雇主和工人习惯了工资增长的模式。 然后,生产力突然停止增长。 然而,人们认识到生产力不再提高,这有延误或滞后。 因此,工资与以往一样不断上升,但劳动力需求不再增长,因此,在W3工资和W4工资中,如果劳动力供应量超过要求的数量,就存在失业。(b) 一段时间以来,生产率的增长率为零,因此雇主和工人开始接受平衡工资水平(W)。 然后,生产率意外地上升,劳动力需求从D0转移到D1. 按工资计算(W),这意味着所需劳动力数量超过所提供数量,而且只要提供大量工作,失业率就会低。
